text:
Mira: thinking out loud: we need a pattern for intent-scoped keys vs operator tokens. goal: retain isolation without blowing up latency.
Juan: agree. batch importer showed direct-claims are fastest but leak origin org into downstream logs. operator tokens hide origin but require broker logic.
Alex: idea: introduce an "intent-scoped API key" that carries minimal org info (org id hashed) + explicit intent. RBAC checks use intent+role instead of full org claim.
Kevin: hashed org is tricky for billing and rate limits. we still need a reliable attribution for quota. maybe include an attribution header injected by gateway after policy eval?
infra-bot: policy deploy: intent-policy v0.3 -> canary applied to /v1/ingest routes (no errors)
Sam: sample JWT we prototyped (for the intent-key path):
```json
{"sub":"svc-ingest","intent":"ingest:write","org_hash":"sha256:abcd...","exp":1780000000}
```
Mira: thanks. question: how do we migrate existing API keys? options: 1) accept legacy keys and route them through operator-bridge when org hiding is needed, 2) mint intent-keys and require rotation.
Juan: operational cost: operator-bridge produces per-request ephemeral operator tokens for mixed-org queues which multiplies token churn. Not great for high-throughput paths.
Alex: propose hybrid routing rules at gateway: fast-path (direct claim) for single-tenant pinned routes; intent-path (hashed org + intent) for multi-tenant public endpoints; operator-bridge only for anonymization-required flows.
Kevin: also need to update telemetry: gateway should attach billing metadata (origin_org_id, rate_key) server-side so backends never see raw org claim when using intent-path. That keeps billing accurate while reducing leak surface.
Sam: SDK changes: client-side should optionally validate server-provided header "x-intent-bound" before calling long-running jobs. Fallbacks: 6-month acceptance window for legacy keys, with automated rotation nudges.
Mira: open concerns: 1) RBAC granularity (intent namespace explode), 2) policy complexity in gateway, 3) migration UX.
Juan: action: I'll draft a whitelist of routes that must stay direct-claims. Alex: can you enumerate services that can accept hashed-org attribution? Kevin: I'll sketch the billing header format and TTL semantics. Sam: I'll write the mini-migration RFC and include sample nginx-lua header rewrite snippet.
Alex: one more: cost of intent-list explosion. we should allow grouping (eg ingest:write -> ingest) in checks for easier role authoring.
Mira: agreed. if we can group intent prefixes in RBAC, that reduces combinatorial growth. next: Sam ping infra for proxy hooks and we'll review the mini-RFC next Tuesday. :thumbsup:
